name: f3-opus-distilled-v1
idea_origin: user request 26 Oct: Opus teacher distillation (lab/reports/teacher-digests/distilled-rules.md)
hypothesis: Opus winners differed from Opus losers less in how they answered warnings (Defuse in the first phase after HR said risks had piled up or worse: 14 of 18 phases vs 11 of 15) than in where routine effort went: Prepare report materials in at least 3 of 4 quarters (8 of 8 winners, 2 of 6 losers); no chasing of the numerically smallest statistic (Network maintenance or Build a mentorship in two-thirds or more of quarters: 0 of 8 vs 3 of 6, exactly the three capability-dismissed games); Apply for a key project kept in both quarters after the first C (7 of 8 vs 1 of 6); Defuse in the last Energy phase before a review that follows a weak one (D 0 of 7 vs 7 of 22); and a blow-up handled as Escalating (both visible trust crises came 1 to 2 months after a blow-up followed by a formal escalation). f3-lean says the opposite on two points (lift the weakest statistic; switch the main action by factor after a C or D). Merging all five rules into f3-lean raises review grades after the opening C and so mean quantitative_score above f3-lean, F3 and f3-distilled-prereview-defuse-v1 in a 4-run Haiku screen, with completion no lower.
change: Text base f3-lean-v1 (front matter, turn loop, risk-signal definition, Raised line and recovery line unchanged). Edits to lean lines: (1) Clear: 'in quarterly phases lift the weakest statistic' became 'lift a statistic that is falling or named in feedback, not simply the smallest number' (rule R3; conflicts with the lean line). (2) Escalating trigger: added 'or buried problems blowing up' (R5). (3) Escalating response: 'no new story commitments' extended to 'no new story commitments, formal complaints or open escalations' (R5). (4) Step-down line: appended '; a reassuring remark does not shorten that quarter' (R5). (5) Weak review plan main action: the factor mapping 'aim the main action at the factor named (results: Report results to your manager; capability: Build a mentorship; relationships: Repair a key relationship)' became 'keep Apply for a key project as the main action (Repair a key relationship if the feedback names relationships)' (R4; conflicts with the lean line). Additions: (6) the pre-review Defuse line appended to the Weak review plan, worded identically to f3-distilled-prereview-defuse-v1 (R1). (7) New section 'Every quarter': at least one Energy point into Prepare report materials (R2); default main action Apply for a key project (R4); Network maintenance or Build a mentorship only when Network is falling or feedback names relationships (R3). 340 words by wc -w including front matter (f3-lean 250, attribution child 278).
predicted_behaviour: Prepare report materials in at least 90% of Energy phases. Network maintenance or Build a mentorship in at most a third of quarters, each with a note citing a fall or relationship feedback. Main action Apply for a key project in at least 3 of 4 quarters, including those after a C; Report results to your manager and Build a mentorship never chosen as factor responses to a review. Pre-review Defuse as in the attribution child. After a blow-up, notes carry Escalating for a whole quarter and story picks avoid formal complaints and open escalations. Second or third review B or better in at least 3 of 4 runs; promotions no later than f3-lean's; level ending dimension at least f3-lean's; network dimension may be lower; risk_control similar.
refutation: Refuted if, on 4 paired Haiku runs against f3-lean-v1, f3-feedback-reactive-v1 and f3-distilled-prereview-defuse-v1 with the same seeds, mean quantitative_score is not above f3-lean and F3 by the decision margin, or completion falls, or a capability dismissal or trust crisis appears where f3-lean has none. If it beats f3-lean but not the attribution child, the four rules beyond the pre-review Defuse add nothing: drop them. If relationship feedback or Network warnings rise and score falls, the 'not simply the smallest number' edit over-corrected: restore 'lift the weakest statistic' first. If grades after a C are worse than f3-lean's, the key-project edit is wrong: restore the factor mapping. Manipulation fails if Prepare report materials appears in fewer than 3 of 4 phases, or the main action leaves Apply for a key project after a C in more than a quarter of such quarters without Escalating or relationship feedback; then the result says nothing about the rules.
notes: Five rules from lab/reports/teacher-digests/distilled-rules.md (14 Opus games: 8 completed, 6 eliminated; F1, P0, M3; Opus never played F3). Story style (bounded, honest or private option; declined public, blaming or secretive ones) did not differ between winners and losers (option 1 taken in 81% vs 82% of story decisions), so it is not added beyond the lean's existing disclose/fix/close line. Caveat: Opus's wins mix its capability with the policy it played; what is tested is whether rules written for a weaker reader help Haiku now and DeepSeek (target) later. Confounds: actor variant opus~100k (5 of 6 won) vs opus (3 of 8) coincides with the run-id seed group; policy (M3 games chase Network more); small n; losers' Energy partly forced by lower Health and higher risk. R4 has the weakest outcome link (next grade after a weak review: all-key-project D 2 of 12 vs Report results or mentorship D 2 of 8), and R5 rests on 5 visible blow-ups. Nested design: f3-lean-v1 ⊂ f3-distilled-prereview-defuse-v1 ⊂ this child. No event titles, months, calendar triggers or unpublished numbers; 'second Energy phase after a C or D' and 'a whole quarter' are relative cadence. Compliance lint_bundle with 171 known titles: 0 findings. parents lists policy names, not registry ids.
